subject: great skua
title: This Bird Stalls Gannets Mid-Air by Grabbing a Wing, Then Robs Them

scenes.text: This bird knocks a gannet out of the sky by grabbing one wing.
The great skua, Shetland's bonxie. Herring-gull sized, 1.4 metres of wingspan, and afraid of nothing.
It flies up beside a gannet, seizes a wingtip, and the gannet stalls and topples into the sea. The skua keeps attacking until it gives up its fish.
When theft fails, it kills. Skuas eat puffins and seabirds up to herring-gull size. On Unst, one was filmed holding a puffin underwater until it stopped moving.
They've been known to take lambs, and even pony foals. Walk near a nest and they dive-bomb your head, sometimes drawing blood.
Around 48,000 pairs in the world, almost all on a few cold North Atlantic islands. Pirates with a postcode.

description:
The great skua, or bonxie, robs gannets by grabbing a wingtip in mid-air so the bigger bird stalls and falls into the sea, then attacks it until it surrenders its fish.
Great skuas are 50 to 58 cm long with a 125 to 140 cm wingspan and weigh about 1.2 to 1.8 kg. They steal food from gulls, terns and northern gannets, and also kill and eat seabirds up to herring-gull size, puffins included; BBC Springwatch filmed one at Hermaness on Unst, Shetland, holding a puffin underwater until it drowned. They have been known to prey on lambs and pony foals, and they dive-bomb people who approach their nests, sometimes drawing blood. The world population is estimated at about 48,000 breeding pairs, nesting in Scotland, Iceland, the Faroes and Norway.
Would you walk through a skua colony?
first_comment: Grab a wing, stall the gannet, take the fish. Which bird would you call the biggest bully in the sky?
